question: Two men do the same journey by travelling at the speed of 18 km/h and 24 km/h, respectively. If one man takes 20 minutes more than the other man, then the distance (in km) of the total journey is:
solution:
Given:

Speed of one person, S₁ = 18 km/hour

Speed of second person, S₂ = 24 km/hour

T₁ – T₂ = 20 minutes

Formula used:

Speed = Distance/Time

Calculation:

Let the distance be x km.

Time taken by first person

⇒ Time = Distance/Speed

⇒ x/18 hour

Time taken by second person

⇒ x/24 hour

T₁ – T₂ = 20 minutes

⇒ x/18 – x/24 = 20/60

⇒ (4x – 3x)/72 = 1/3

⇒ x = 72/3

⇒ x = 24 km

∴ The distance travelled is 24 km.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0f6448757d2cde942412904dddc23f657eed29e61918cc552d57e9cc685ea3b.png] 

Required distance = {(S₁ × S₂)/(S₂ – S₁)} × (T₁ – T₂)

⇒ {(18 × 24)/(24 – 18)} × (20/60)

⇒ (18 × 24)/6) × (1/3)

⇒ 24 km

∴ The distance travelled is 24 km
